title: 'Nothing' on a value type means its DEFAULT (0/False), not null — 'x = Nothing' is not a null check
sourceContent:
Public Class OrderState
    ' For a VALUE type, `Nothing` is the type's default value (0 for Integer).
    ' `qty = Nothing` is therefore `qty = 0` -- NOT a null check.
    Public Function IsUnset(qty As Integer) As Boolean
        Return qty = Nothing   ' TRUE when qty is 0
    End Function

    ' For a REFERENCE type, `Nothing` IS null.
    Public Sub Reset(ByRef item As Object)
        item = Nothing
    End Sub
End Class
notes: VB.NET overloads `Nothing` to mean both 'null' (reference types) and 'the default value' (value types). `qty = Nothing` on an Integer compiles and means `qty = 0`. A C# port must decide per-site whether the intent was a zero check (`qty == 0`) or genuine nullability (`int?` + `== null`); the two are behaviourally different and the extractor should raise an openQuestion.
